title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 43 (Penalty and Compensation for Damage to Computer)

content.overview: Section 43 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 imposes civil liability: if any person without permission of the owner or any other person who is in charge of a computer, computer system or computer network accesses or secures access, downloads, copies or extracts data, introduces a contaminant or virus, damages or disrupts, denies access, charges services to another’s account, destroys or alters information, steals or conceals or alters source code, or does other listed acts, he is liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person affected. Section 43 is civil; criminal liability for dishonest/fraudulent commission of s. 43 acts is under s. 66.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Was a listed act done? (2) Without permission of owner/person in charge? (3) Computer resource nexus under s. 2? (4) Civil compensation vs s. 66 criminal?
content.study:
s. 43 does not require criminal mens rea. s. 66 adds dishonestly or fraudulently for criminal punishment. List the specific clause of s. 43 on the facts.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Civil liability
sections.body: Listed acts without permission attract liability to pay damages by way of compensation to the affected person.

sections.heading: Listed acts
sections.body: Include unauthorised access, downloading/copying data, introducing virus/contaminant, causing damage/disruption, denial of access, charging services to another account, destroying/altering information, and source-code related acts — as enumerated in the section.

sections.heading: Without permission
sections.body: The act must be without permission of the owner or person in charge of the computer, system or network.

sections.heading: vs s. 66
sections.body: s. 66 criminalises doing any act under s. 43 dishonestly or fraudulently; s. 43 remains the civil compensation path.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify listed act; prove lack of permission; quantify compensation claim; consider parallel s. 66 if mens rea present.

provisions.title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.

examples.title: Unauthorised data copy
examples.body: Employee copies confidential database without permission after exit — s. 43 civil claim for compensation; s. 66 if done dishonestly/fraudulently.

hypotheticals.question: Must prosecution prove dishonesty for s. 43 compensation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 43 is civil compensation for listed acts without permission; dishonesty is relevant to s. 66 criminal liability.

distinctions.title: s. 43 civil vs s. 66 criminal
distinctions.left: Compensation for listed acts without permission.
distinctions.right: Punishment when s. 43 acts are done dishonestly or fraudulently.

misconceptions.trap: s. 43 is only a criminal provision.
misconceptions.correction: s. 43 is civil compensation; criminal path is s. 66 for dishonest/fraudulent commission.
